title: Why Does Netflix Keep Raising Its Price?
description:
Netflix went from $7.99 in 2011 to $19.99 for Standard today, and its cheapest plan now has ads and still costs more than the whole service did back then.
#netflix #streaming #money #shorts

Sources: TheWrap (Mar 26, 2026); FOX Television Stations (Mar 27, 2026); BGR (2026); Android Authority price timeline; Looper; Antenna data via Business Insider (Mar 2026) and MediaPost; Netflix ad-revenue outlook via TheWrap and DesignRush (2026)
Photos: rawpixel (CC0), Marit & Toomas Hinnosaar, brianc, stockcatalog, nan palmero (CC BY 2.0, Flickr)
first_comment: Be honest: at $19.99, are you keeping Netflix or canceling? 📺

scenes.say: Netflix now costs two and a half times what it did.
scenes.source: $7.99 streaming-only in 2011 (Android Authority timeline; Looper 'each costing $8/month') -> $19.99 Standard after the March 2026 hike (TheWrap Mar 26 2026; FOX Mar 27 2026; BGR 2026). 19.99 / 7.99 = 2.50

scenes.say: In {2011|twenty eleven}, streaming Netflix was {$7.99|seven ninety nine} a month.
scenes.source: Android Authority timeline (2011: $7.99 streaming plan); Looper (2011 DVD and streaming split, 'each costing $8/month')

scenes.say: {$7.99|Seven ninety nine} then. {$19.99|Nineteen ninety nine} for Standard today.
scenes.source: TheWrap Mar 26 2026 (Standard now $19.99, up $2); FOX Mar 27 2026 (Standard $19.99, previously $17.99); BGR 2026 (March 2026: Standard from $17.99 to $19.99)

scenes.say: You'd think people would cancel. But only about two in a hundred quit each month.
scenes.source: Antenna via Business Insider/iTiger Mar 27 2026 ('averaging around 2% monthly compared with 6% to 8% for many other services, according to data firm Antenna'); MediaPost 'Netflix Monthly Subscriber Churn Still Lowest At 2%'

scenes.say: Rivals lose three or four times as many.
scenes.source: Antenna via Business Insider/iTiger Mar 2026: Netflix ~2% vs 6-8% for many other services = 3-4x

scenes.say: So how does Netflix get away with it? The hikes come one or two dollars at a time.
But here's the interesting part. The cheapest plan now has ads.
scenes.source: TheWrap Mar 2026 (Standard With Ads now $8.99); FOX Mar 2026 (Standard with Ads $8.99/month)

scenes.say: And at {$8.99|eight ninety nine}, it costs more than all of Netflix did in {2011|twenty eleven}.
scenes.source: $8.99 ads plan (TheWrap; FOX, Mar 2026) vs $7.99 streaming in 2011 (Android Authority; Looper)

scenes.say: Those ads should bring in {$3 BILLION|three billion dollars} this year, double last year.
scenes.source: TheWrap Mar 2026 (Netflix projects ad revenue will double to $3 billion from $1.5 billion in 2025); DesignRush 'Netflix Ad Revenue Set to Hit $3 Billion in 2026'; PPC Land Q1 2026 ('ads business chases $3B target')

scenes.say: So Netflix gets paid twice: once by you, once by advertisers.
scenes.source: Subscription price (TheWrap/FOX) + ad revenue (TheWrap/DesignRush) on the ads plan
